title: Brown butter cinnamon rolls
author: Sunday baker
summary: Soft morning rolls with a brown-butter cinnamon filling and a thin vanilla glaze. They ask for a slow morning and a warm oven.
ingredients: 1/3 cup sugar, plus 2 tablespoons for the filling
6 tablespoons butter, browned, plus 2 tablespoons soft butter
1 cup powdered sugar and 2 tablespoons milk for the glaze
steps: Stir the yeast into the warm milk with a pinch of the sugar. Let it sit until foamy.
Mix in the remaining dough sugar, egg, yolk, salt, and 2 tablespoons of the brown butter. Add the flour and knead until the dough is smooth and slightly tacky.
Cover and let the dough rise until doubled, about an hour in a warm kitchen.
Stir the cinnamon and 2 tablespoons of sugar into the rest of the brown butter.
Roll the dough into a rectangle, spread the filling to the edges, and roll it up from the long side. Cut into 12 pieces and set them in a buttered pan.
Let them puff again for 30 minutes. Bake at 350°F until the tops are golden, about 22 minutes.
Whisk the powdered sugar with milk and a splash of vanilla. Spoon it over the warm rolls.

title: Skillet honey cornbread
author: Weeknight cook
summary: A cast-iron cornbread with a crisp edge and a tender middle. Honey goes in the batter and again on the hot squares.
ingredients: 1/4 cup honey, plus more for the table
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Put the butter in a 10-inch skillet and set the skillet in the oven until the butter melts and starts to smell nutty.
Whisk the cornmeal, flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt.
Whisk the buttermilk, eggs, and honey. Stir the wet mixture into the dry until just combined, then fold in most of the melted butter, leaving a slick in the skillet.
Pour the batter into the hot skillet. Bake until the top is deep gold and a toothpick comes out clean, about 20 minutes.
Cool for 10 minutes. Cut into wedges and pass more honey.

title: Roasted tomato bread soup
summary: Tomatoes roasted until they slump, blended with a torn heel of bread so the soup turns silky without cream.
author: The soup pot
ingredients: 2 thick slices of day-old bread, torn
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the tomatoes, onion, and garlic with the olive oil and a good pinch of salt. Roast until the tomatoes collapse and the edges char, about 35 minutes.
Squeeze the garlic from its skins. Blend the vegetables with the broth and bread until mostly smooth. Leave a little texture if you like.
Pour the soup into a pot and simmer 10 minutes. Season with pepper and more salt.
Ladle into warm bowls and tear basil over the top.
